scope: Full contextual source review of VCFv4.5 structural-variant INFO definitions, tandem-repeat INFO semantics, SV FORMAT semantics and the complete complex-rearrangement/breakend section. The verbatim line excerpts are retained for review traceability; normative force is not inferred from examples or change-log prose.
method: Read complete contiguous source sections, not isolated candidate lines.
Retain adjacent definitions, modal wording, examples and explicit cross-references.
Separate MUST/must, should, may/recommendation, implementation-defined behaviour and examples.
Do not infer parser implementation requirements from examples unless the prose establishes the rule.
Treat source change-log entries as explanatory deltas, not replacements for normative section text.

source_excerpt: 844: The following INFO keys are reserved for encoding structural variants.
845: In general, when these keys are used by imprecise variants, the values should be best estimates.
846: When present, per allele values must be specified for all ALT alleles (including non-structural alleles).
847: Except in lists of strings, the missing value should be used as a placeholder for the ALT alleles for which the key does not have a meaningful value.
848: The empty string should be used to encode missing values in lists of strings.
856: Indicates that this record contains an imprecise structural variant $ALT$ allele. ALT alleles missing $CIPOS$ are to be interpreted as imprecise variants with an unspecified confidence interval.
858: If a precise ALT allele is present in a record with the $IMPRECISE$ flag, $CIPOS$ must be explicitly set for that allele, even if it is `0,0`.
863: ##INFO=<ID=END,Number=1,Type=Integer,Description="Deprecated. Present for backwards compatibility with earlier versions of VCF.">
867: $END$ has been deprecated in favour of INFO SVLEN and FORMAT LEN.
876: This field has been deprecated due to redundancy with ALT.
877: Refer to section \ref{altfield} for the set of valid ALT field symbolic structural variant alleles.
885: One value for each ALT allele.
887: SVLEN must be specified for symbolic structural variant alleles.
888: SVLEN is defined for $INS$, $DUP$, $INV$, and $DEL$ symbolic alleles as the number of the inserted, duplicated, inverted, and deleted bases respectively.
889: SVLEN is defined for $CNV$ symbolic alleles as the length of the segment over which the copy number variant is defined.
890: The missing value $.$ should be used for all other ALT alleles, including ALT alleles using breakend notation.
892: For backwards compatibility, a missing SVLEN should be inferred from the $END$ field.
894: For backwards compatibility, the absolute value of SVLEN should be taken and a negative SVLEN should be treated as positive values.
896: Note that for structural variant symbolic alleles, $POS$ corresponds to the base immediately preceding the variant.
900: ##INFO=<ID=CIPOS,Number=.,Type=Integer,Description="Confidence interval around POS for symbolic structural variants">
904: If present, the number of entries must be twice the number of ALT alleles.
905: $CIPOS$ consists of successive pairs of records indicating the start and end offsets relative to $POS$ of the confidence interval for each ALT allele.
906: For example, $CIPOS=-5,5,0,0$ indicates a 5bp confidence interval in each direction for the first ALT allele, and an exact position for the second alt allele.
908: When breakpoint sequence homology exists, $CIPOS$ should be used in conjunction with $HOMSEQ$ to specify the interval of homology.
910: If both $IMPRECISE$ and $CIPOS$ are omitted, $CIPOS$ is implicitly defined as 0,0 for all alleles.
912: Each $CIPOS$ interval must span 0. That is, the lower bound cannot be greater than 0, and the upper bound cannot be less than 0.
916: ##INFO=<ID=CIEND,Number=.,Type=Integer,Description="Confidence interval around the inferred END for symbolic structural variants">
920: If present, the number of entries must be twice the number of ALT alleles.
921: $CIEND$ consists of successive pairs of records encoding the confidence interval start and end offsets relative to the $END$ position inferred by $SVLEN$ for each ALT allele.
922: For symbolic structural variants, the first in the pair must not be greater than 0, and the second must not be less than 0.
923: For all other alleles, both should be the missing value $.$.
924: For example, $CIEND=-5,5,.,.$ indicates a 5bp confidence interval in each direction around the end position for the first ALT allele, and no $CIEND$ is defined for the second alt allele.
926: If $CIEND$ is missing, it is assumed to match $CIPOS$.

944: However, the alternate allele assembly file may contain additional information about the characteristics of the alt allele contigs.

976: Whilst simple events such as deletions and duplications can be wholly represented by a single VCF record, complex rearrangements such as chromothripsis result in a large number of breakpoints.
977: VCF uses the $EVENT$ field to group such related records together, and $EVENTTYPE$ to classify these events.
978: All records with the same $EVENT$ value are considered to be part of the same event.
980: The following $EVENTTYPE$ values are reserved and should be used when appropriate:
984:   \item DEL:ME - Deletion of mobile element with respect to the reference
999: The semantics of other $EVENTTYPE$ values is implementation-defined.
1000: The use of $EVENT$ is not restricted to structural variation and can also be used to associate non-symbolic alleles.
1001: Such linking is useful for scenarios such as kataegis or when there is variant position ambiguity in segmentally duplicated regions.
1009: If present, the number of entries must be twice the number of ALT alleles.
1010: $CILEN$ consists of successive pairs of records indicating the lower and upper bounds of the $SVLEN$ confidence interval.
1019: If present, the number of entries must be twice the number of ALT alleles.
1020: $CICN$ consists of successive pairs of records indicating the lower and upper copy number bounds.
1024: ##INFO=<ID=SVCLAIM,Number=A,Type=String,Description="Claim made by the structural variant call. Valid values are D, J, DJ for abundance, adjacency and both respectively">
1028: This field disambiguates the claim being made by DEL and DUP structural variants.

1030: The distinction between different claim types is made necessary by the fact that many structural variants affect both the overall abundance of a region and its adjacency structure, but often only one of those effects is being directly observed.
1031: It is important to specify which one, because if this is not done, other variants in a genome may make the call ambiguous.

1033: For example, a ``conventional'' deletion usually both decreases the DNA abundance of a region and creates an adjacency between two sequence locations, which are the breakpoints of that deletion.
1034: However, if a deletion or duplication is accompanied by a compensatory variant elsewhere in the genome, it may only cause changes in the adjacency structure, but not the overall copy number.
1035: On the contrary, combinations of certain complex events in a genome may cause the overall copy number decrease, but not the linear excision of a sequence fragment.
1037: A copy number based duplication call does not make any claims on where the duplicated region is in the genome.
1038: It could be a simple tandem duplication, a dispersed duplication, retrotransposition, or even form part of extra-chromosomal DNA such as a double minute.
1039: In contrast, a breakpoint based duplication call requires that the end of the duplicated region be adjacent to the start of the duplicated region.
1040: This rules out events such as dispersed duplication or retrotransposition, but is consistent with simple tandem duplications as well as double minutes.
1041: Both deletion and duplication breakpoint calls can form part of more complex events that result in no copy number change in the deleted/duplicated region.
1043: To resolve any ambiguity in the interpretation of deletion and duplication symbolic alleles, three claim types are defined:

1046:   \item D (abun\textbf{\emph{d}}ance / read \textbf{\emph{D}}epth) claim indicates that the call has been made based only on a measure of DNA abundance of the called region, with no evidence to support changes in breakpoint structure. This includes indirect claims of abundance made using SNV variant allele frequency.

1047:   \item J (ad\textbf{\emph{j}}acency / break \textbf{\emph{J}}unction) claim indicates that the call has been made based on the detection of a non-reference DNA adjacency, with no evidence to support overall changes in DNA abundance.
1048:   \item DJ indicates that there is evidence for both DNA abundance and adjacency changes, which are consistent with each other and suggest the structural variant of the type being reported.
1051: Rules of applying SVCLAIM field are different depending on symbolic allele type:
1054:   \item DEL/DUP: SVCLAIM must be specified and can be be D, J, or DJ. J and DJ claims indicate a breakpoint between the start and end of the DEL/DUP.
1055:   \item CNV: implicit abundance claim (SVCLAIM=D). SVCLAIM is optional but, if specified, must be D, or the missing value ``.'', which is equivalent to D.
1056:   \item INV/INS: implicit adjacency claims (SVCLAIM=J). SVCLAIM is optional but, if specified, must be J, DJ, or the missing value ``.'', which is equivalent to J.
1057:   \item breakend alleles are implicit adjacency claims (SVCLAIM=J). SVCLAIM is optional but, if specified, must be J, or the missing value ``.'', which is equivalent to J.
1058:   \item Non-SV alleles should use the missing value ``.''.
1061: If all alleles contain the missing value ``.'', the SVCLAIM field can be omitted.
1063: Note that the scope of SVCLAIM is the single ALT allele taken in isolation.
1064: Complex events such as a cut and paste transposition of a mobile element result in multiple interrelated copy number and breakpoint claims.
1065: These records should be linked using EVENT/EVENTTYPE, with the SVCLAIM field on each record specifying the claim of that individual allele record.

1066: That is, a J claim must not be made on a CNV record even if the corresponding start/end breakpoints are known, and a DJ claim on a DEL or DUP is a claim of a simple, isolated deletion or tandem duplication.

source_excerpt: 1070: ##INFO=<ID=RN,Number=A,Type=Integer,Description="Total number of repeat sequences in this allele">
1074: Used by $<$CNV:TR$>$ tandem repeat alleles to encode the number of repeat sequences.
1075: This field determines the number of values encoded in the RUS, RUL, RB, CIRB, RUC and CIRUC fields for each allele.
1076: The length of these fields must match the sum of all RN values for the record.
1077: For the purposes of determining RUS, RUL, RB, CIRB, RUC and CIRUC lengths, the missing value ``.'' should be treated as 0.
1078: If this field is missing, the RN for each $<$CNV:TR$>$ allele is assumed to be 1 and 0 otherwise.
1084: ##INFO=<ID=RUS,Number=.,Type=String,Description="Repeat unit sequence of the corresponding repeat sequence">
1085: ##INFO=<ID=RUL,Number=.,Type=Integer,Description="Repeat unit length of the corresponding repeat sequence">
1086: ##INFO=<ID=RUC,Number=.,Type=Float,Description="Repeat unit count of corresponding repeat sequence">
1087: ##INFO=<ID=RB,Number=.,Type=Integer,Description="Total number of bases in the corresponding repeat sequence">
1091: Used by $<$CNV:TR$>$ tandem repeat alleles to encode information about the nature of the tandem repeats contained for ALT alleles.
1092: Conceptually, these fields each contain a list of values for each ALT allele.
1093: The length of these inner lists are determined by the RN field for that ALT allele and the length must match the sum of RN for the record.
1094: These fields contain the flattened and concatenated list contents in the same order as either corresponding ALT allele.
1096: Each $<$CNV:TR$>$ allele consists of $RN$ repeat sequences each containing $RUC$ repeat units with sequence $RUS$.

1098: For example, if a $<$CNV:TR$>$ allele sequence is $(CAG)_{10}(TG)_{7}(CAGG)_{3}$, the RN for that ALT allele would be 3, the RUS $CAG,TG,CAGG$, the RUL $3,2,4$, the RUC $10,7,3$ and the RB $30,14,12$.
1100: RUS may contain only IUPAC nucleotide codes (ambiguous bases are allowed) or the missing value (`.').
1101: If both RUS and RUL are present and not missing, the length of each RUS entry must match the corresponding RUL.
1102: If both RUC and RB are present and not missing, RB should approximately equal RUL*RUC but is not required to match exactly.
1103: If RUS is present but RUL is not, RUL should be inferred to be equal to the length of the corresponding RUS.
1105: See section \ref{tandem-repeats} for an example and further details.
1115: Confidence interval around RUC and RB respectively.
1116: The length of these fields must be twice that of their corresponding fields.
1117: CIRUC/CIRB must not be non-missing for any alleles with no corresponding RUC/RB value.
1119: These fields are defined in the same manner as $CIPOS$ and contain the difference between the lower and upper confidence interval bounds and the value of the corresponding field.
1120: The lower bound must be less than or equal to zero and the upper bound must be greater than or equal to zero.
1121: If the lower bound is the missing value ``.'', is assumed to be 0 and if the upper bound is the missing value ``.'', it is assumed to be an unbounded estimate.
1122: That is, the length of repeat has been determined to be at least a certain length but a reasonable limit of total length of the repeat could not be determined.
1124: See section \ref{tandem-repeats} for an example and further details.
1128: ##INFO=<ID=RUB,Number=.,Type=Integer,Description="Number of bases in each individual repeat unit">
1132: This field encodes the length of each repeat unit for situations where the length of each repeat unit varies greatly.
1133: If this field is present, RUC must also be present and must contain only integer values.
1134: This field uses the same list-of-list encoding as RUS/RUL/RUC/RB but contains a list for each RC entry, the length of which is determined by the corresponding integer RUC value.
1135: This field contains the length of each individual repeat unit for each RUC entry.
1136: If RUB is missing or not specified, the $RUB$ for each individual repeat unit is considered to be equal to the $RUL$ for the corresponding repeat sequence.
1138: For the vast majority of tandem repeats, this field can be omitted and is only required in complex situations such as when a VNTR contains one or more variable length STRs.
1140: See section \ref{tandem-repeats} for an example and further details.

source_excerpt: 1151: ##FORMAT=<ID=NQ,Number=1,Type=Integer,Description="Phred style probability score that the variant is novel">
1156: CN specifies the total copy number over the region defined in the $<$CNV$>$, $<$DEL$>$, $<$DUP$>$ alleles.
1157: When FORMAT CN is present, all $<$CNV$>$, $<$DEL$>$ and $<$DUP$>$ alleles must have the same SVLEN.
1158: CNQ, CNL, and CNP are analogous to GQ/GL/GP fields.
1159: CNQ is encoded as a phred quality $-10log_{10}$ p(copy number genotype call is wrong).
1160: CNL specifies a list of $log_{10}$ likelihoods for each potential copy number, starting from zero.
1161: CNP is 0 to 1-scaled copy number posterior probabilities (and otherwise defined precisely as the CNL field), intended to store imputed genotype probabilities.
1162: When possible, GT/GQ/GL/GP should be used instead of (or in addition to) these keys.

source_excerpt: 1397: An arbitrary rearrangement can be summarized as a set of novel \textbf{adjacencies}. Each adjacency ties together $2$ \textbf{breakends}.
1398: The two breakends at either end of a novel adjacency are called \textbf{mates}.
1400: There is one line of VCF (i.e.\ one record) for each of the two breakends in a novel adjacency.
1401: The REF field of a breakend record indicates a base or sequence s of bases beginning at position POS, as in all VCF records.
1402: The ALT field of a breakend record indicates a replacement for s.
1405:   \item The string t that replaces places s.
1406:   The string t may be an extended version of s if some novel bases are inserted during the formation of the novel adjacency.
1407:   \item The position p of the mate breakend, indicated by a string of the form ``chr:pos''.
1408:   This is the location of the first mapped base in the piece being joined at this novel adjacency.
1409:   \item The direction that the joined sequence continues in, starting from p.
1410:   This is indicated by the orientation of square brackets surrounding p.
1413: These 3 elements are combined in 4 possible ways to create the ALT.
1414: In each of the 4 cases, the assertion is that s is replaced with t, and then some piece starting at position p is joined to t.
1420: s & t$[$p$[$ & piece extending to the right of p is joined after t \\
1421: s & t$]$p$]$ & reverse comp piece extending left of p is joined after t \\
1422: s & $]$p$]$t & piece extending to the left of p is joined before t \\
1423: s & $[$p$[$t & reverse comp piece extending right of p is joined before t \\
1427: The example in Figure 1 shows a 3-break operation involving 6 breakends.
1428: It exemplifies all possible orientations of breakends in adjacencies.
1429: Notice how the ALT field expresses the orientation of the breakends.

contextual_findings.finding: The section introduces reserved SV INFO keys. For imprecise variants values should be best estimates. When present, per-allele values must cover every ALT, including non-SV alleles. Missing-value placeholders are required for ALT alleles without meaningful values, except list-of-string missing entries use empty strings.

IMPRECISE is a presence flag. An ALT lacking CIPOS is interpreted as imprecise with unspecified CI. In a record carrying IMPRECISE, any precise ALT must carry explicit CIPOS including 0,0. END is deprecated in favour of SVLEN and FORMAT LEN; SVTYPE is deprecated as redundant with ALT.

SVLEN has one value per ALT; it is required for symbolic SV alleles; its meaning is class-specific; other ALT forms including breakend notation receive missing. Backwards compatibility permits inference from END when missing and absolute-value interpretation of negative values. POS for symbolic SVs is the base immediately preceding the variant.

CIPOS and CIEND are ALT-paired offset vectors. CIPOS pairs are relative to POS and must span zero. CIEND pairs are relative to END inferred from SVLEN; symbolic bounds span zero and non-symbolic alleles are missing. Missing CIEND is assumed to match CIPOS. If both IMPRECISE and CIPOS are omitted, CIPOS is implicitly 0,0 for all alleles.

HOMLEN and HOMSEQ describe breakpoint microhomology; precise alternate-allele assembly can be derived from REF/ALT, but assembly files may carry additional alternate-contig characteristics. No unsupported requirement should be inferred about assembly file existence.
MEINFO and METRANS are per-ALT four-element tuples with fixed semantic order; tuple cardinality is four times ALT count.

DGVID/DBVARID/DBRIPID, MATEID/PARID/EVENT/EVENTTYPE are ALT-indexed. EVENT groups records; EVENTTYPE classifies event. Reserved EVENTTYPE values are recommended when appropriate; other values are implementation-defined. EVENT may link non-SV alleles too.

CILEN/CICN are paired confidence bounds; CN is per-ALT copy number; SVCLAIM disambiguates abundance and adjacency assertions with class-dependent allowed values and implicit claims. SVCLAIM scope is each ALT independently; complex events are linked with EVENT/EVENTTYPE.

Tandem-repeat RN controls nested list cardinality. Missing RN is treated as zero in length sums; absent RN defaults to one for CNV:TR and zero otherwise. RUS/RUL/RUC/RB values flatten concatenated per-ALT lists. RB approximately equals RUL×RUC but exact equality is not required. CIRUC/CIRB encode signed offsets. RUB is a nested per-repeat-unit list dependent on RUC, with RUL as its absent-field default.

FORMAT CN is sample-specific total copy number over the segment defined by CNV/DEL/DUP. When present, all such alleles in the record must share SVLEN. CNQ/CNL/CNP are copy-number analogues of genotype quality/likelihood/posterior; the source says standard GT/GQ/GL/GP should be used instead of or in addition when possible.

A novel adjacency connects two breakends called mates and has one record per breakend. REF is sequence starting at POS; ALT replaces it with t plus mate coordinate and bracket-encoded direction. Exactly four bracket arrangements define the orientation of joined sequence.

Inserted sequence may be included in ALT; large inserted sequence may be represented by an assembly contig. Complete insertion of a sequence between two base pairs has a recommended symbolic-contig shorthand. Partial contig insertion uses a specified contig interval. Circular contig insertion requires an additional circular adjacency.

A breakend with multiple mates represents alternative adjacencies as alternate alleles. Partner breakends are distinct from mates; each breakend has one partner, and PARID may name the partner explicitly.
Virtual telomeric breakends are defined at coordinate 0 and N+1 for a reference chromosome spanning 1..N, providing a partner for telomeric breakends.

EVENT can group all adjacencies in a rearrangement. A simple inversion may use symbolic shorthand or explicit breakends. Under microhomology uncertainty, the breakend is placed arbitrarily at the leftmost position and CIPOS records uncertainty. Mate coordinates in ALT are conditional on the selected local breakend position; MATEID maintains mate identity and PARID may express partner relationships.
